html:
Borscht is a sour soup, usually red from beetroot, eaten across eastern Europe and seen as the national dish of Ukraine, with written mentions from the 1500s.

The name comes from the hogweed plant once used to make it; beetroot became the base later. Ukrainian borscht is made with beets, cabbage, potatoes and often meat, soured with fermented beet juice or vinegar, and served with sour cream and garlic buns called pampushky. Each region and family has its own version. In Poland a clear red barszcz is served at Christmas Eve, and Russians also claim the soup. In July 2022, during the Russian invasion, UNESCO added the culture of Ukrainian borscht cooking to its list of heritage in urgent need of protection. It is part of the everyday life of Ukraine.
sum: Borscht is a sour soup, usually red from beetroot, eaten across eastern Europe and seen as the national dish of Ukraine, with written mentions from the 1500s.
